column11: judgement, set against what an adult preventive has done: the RSV vaccines reached 6,522,057 Medicare Part D beneficiaries in their first season, 5.9% of Merck's 110 million high-risk pool (mrk_cd388_injection.csv, CMS Part D 2023). The ceiling is willingness: 64% of residents of Connecticut, Maryland, Minnesota and New York would take a Lyme vaccine, 30% were uncertain (Hook SA et al., Vaccine 2022;40(2):298-305, doi 10.1016/j.vaccine.2021.11.065)
column12: 2% of the unvaccinated pool a year, a third of the RSV vaccines' first-season pace and level with CD388. Against it: four doses rather than one, a missed primary statistical criterion that may narrow any recommendation, a pool that counts everyone in a risk area, 68% of US providers willing to recommend in 2022, down from 73% in 2018 (Bostic TD et al., Vaccine 2025, doi 10.1016/j.vaccine.2025.127495), and LYMErix, withdrawn three years after its 1998 approval amid declining sales (Nigrovic LE, Thompson KM, Epidemiol Infect 2007;135(1):1-8). For it: nothing is displaced, as no Lyme vaccine is sold, and a vaccine ACIP recommends carries no cost sharing for most insured patients. The build peaks at $1,461mm in 2032 with ex-US, about 1.57 million US courses a year, and by 2046 has vaccinated about 31% of the US pool, under half the 64% who say they are willing. Valneva's 20-F (0001628280-26-018808) estimates the global market for a Lyme vaccine to exceed $1 billion, which this sits above; at 1.5% the peak is $1,111mm

column11: derived: Pfizer generated $23,703mm of free cash flow on $185,759mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 12.76% margin, against the 33.8% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%.
